provisionalNote: A critic visual pass (seven lenses plus skeptic verification), not a deep round: provisional scores for visual, feel and interface only; no obligation is settled and the weighted total is not recomputed.
request: Bailey, 2026-10-01 ~00:20 EDT: "I need another pass on visuals and maxing out eye candy with special emphasis on character models, enemy models, animations, visual fidelity, and camera perspective in relation to characters, enemies, and the battlefield as a whole. The critic needs to be involved as well and I need updated scores."
summary: Provisional critic visual pass on release 33 (main f302f163, live), seven lenses with skeptic verification, emphasis on character models, enemy models, animation, fidelity and camera. No critical. 16 majors, none a regression against live: the approved spherechange beat is unbuilt (FFX-2), party and enemies interpenetrate on screen in 9-12 chapters against the approved targeting B (both), Den of Woe is far off its approved frame (FFX-2, D suspected), KO'd FFX-2 girls stand at 0 HP, KO paintings render at the wrong scale (both), hits land after the attacker is home (both), six art identity or coverage gaps (Yuna White Mage costume, Vegnagun Tail, FFX-2 Bahamut, dressphere and boss pose coverage, Seymour Flux approved set), two staging-scale taste majors (Leblanc trio, Ixion plate), the spherechange white card and the Overdrive overlay naming the wrong move (FFX). Provisional scores: visual 8.6 (9.1), feel 7.9 (8.3), interface 7.9 (8.0). Emphasis: character models 7.6, enemy models 7.1, animation 6.2, fidelity 7.9, camera 7.5. 16 eye-candy gaps ranked by payoff, led by living idle motion and art in the blank aeon/boss splash slabs.

scores.notes: PROVISIONAL: a visual pass by seven critic lenses on the live release 33 build, not a deep round. It does not settle any obligation, does not recompute the weighted total (combat, encounter, narrative, audio, onboarding, prep and delivery were not judged), and an old score never certifies a new build. VISUAL 8.6 (18b: 9.1). Lens scores: characters 8.4, enemies 8.6, animation 8.6, fidelity 8.6, camera 8.7, scenes-vfx-chrome 8.9, showpiece 8.8; median 8.6. Round 18b scored stills at rest; this pass looked at figures in motion, at 2x and against approved targets, and found open visual majors: two approved-target deviations (party clear of the enemy group, VP-1001-02; Den of Woe O-3 A, VP-1001-03), KO scale (VP-1001-05), identity breaks between paintings (VP-1001-07, -08, -09, -12), the spherechange white card (VP-1001-15), and staging scale (VP-1001-13, -14). That is below the '9 = polished with minor issues' anchor. It stays above 8.5 because resting frames still match the approved tiles, the party is crisp (3.1-4.7 texels/px) and on-model, and eye candy D lifts every scene. The characters lens's 8.4 counted PR-0002 as major (skeptic: polish) and the x-ray ghosting during Overdrive (refuted), so it is weighted down; the scenes lens's 8.9 did not see the pose-identity breaks. FEEL 7.9 (18b: 8.3). Lens scores: 7.9, 8.1, 7.6, 8.2, 8.2, 8.2, 8.0. The animation lens (7.6) and the characters lens (7.9) own motion and carry the most weight here: the approved spherechange beat is missing (major, milestone gate), every hit lands after the attacker is home (major), Overdrives reuse the Attack lunge, idles and casts read as stills, and pose swaps ghost. The calm camera, pinned HUD, per-game hit-stop and canon-aware departures keep it from going lower. INTERFACE 7.9 (18b: 8.0). Five lenses held 8.0; the animation and scenes lenses found one new verified major (the Overdrive overlay names the wrong move, VP-1001-16, FFX) and a run of splash-layer collisions in both games, including the D must-fix 6 that never met its acceptance (VP-1001-32). The four interface majors carried from 18b were not re-judged and are not double-counted.

emphasis.notes: Reconciled from the lenses (owner lens first, others as cross-checks). characterModels 7.6 (lenses 7.4, 6.8, 7.8, 8.4, 8.4, 7.8; owner characters 7.4, raised a little because two of its majors were downgraded or refuted). enemyModels 7.1 (7.0, 6.0, 7.3, 7.9, 8.1, 7.0; owner enemies 7.0). animation 6.2 (6.6, 6.6, 5.4, 7.3, 7.8, 7.9, 6.3; owner animation 5.4, the most thorough measurement; the lenses that scored higher saw motion only incidentally). fidelity 7.9 (8.2, 7.4, 7.8, 8.1, 8.4, 8.0, 7.7; owner fidelity 8.1, lowered for the Den of Woe target deviation that lens did not see). camera 7.5 (7.6, 7.6, 7.4, 7.9, 7.6, 8.3, 7.2; owner camera 7.6).

shipTags: Every critical or major carries introducedByCandidate and regressionVsLive. The candidate is the live build, so nothing is a regression against live. Eye candy D first shipped in this release (commit 2048cdac is not in the previous live 1a6fd3cc), so D-caused items (VP-1001-03 suspected, -17, -22) were introduced by release 33 relative to the build before it; each has its own settings switch.

issues.title: The approved 'spherechange gets its moment' beat is not built: a spherechange is a ~0.47 s white flash and painting swap, with no Full / Short / Off setting
issues.where: Every FFX-2 spherechange (seen Ch IV Bahamut, Ch VI Leblanc), all sizes
issues.detail: Approved tile (Bailey, 19 Sep, polish group, 'FFX-2 only, with the original's short and off options'): a 1.4 s beat with field dim, ribbons, silhouette peak at 0.75 s, named reveal at 1.0 s, HUD back at 1.4 s, and Full / Short / Off with canon's full-the-first-time rule (research/ffx-vs-ffx2-presentation.md §6). Build: BattlePresenterEvents.ts case 'spherechange' does a 420 ms actor flash, a 180 ms screen flash, setArt, the summon cue and sleep(TIMING.status); event logs show turn-start to action-end of about 0.47 s (Bahamut s2 85603.8 to 86070.2; Leblanc 54340 to 54839). No settings row exists. The camera never frames the girl (she is ~30 % of the frame). The tile has no delivery field, so this is an unbuilt approved target and a milestone-gate failure. Found by the characters, animation, camera and showpiece lenses; verified in code and target by two skeptics (high).
issues.fixHint: Confirm with Bailey that the 19 Sep picture is still the target, then build it behind its own switch (default on, D-297): field dim, ribbon VFX in the Spectacle layer, silhouette via the figure tint, serif reveal plate, a cut to a close framing (no swing, D-291), Full / Short / Off with Full forced the first time per girl and dressphere. REDUCE MOTION gives Short with no push.

issues.title: Party and enemies are staged in depth, not across the field: silhouettes interpenetrate at the resting camera in 9 to 12 chapters
issues.where: Resting camera, 1600x900 and 390x844. Edge gap (enemy left minus party right): Evrae -353 px, Ch VII Macalania -328, Yojimbo -221, BFA -153, Yunalesca -120, Bahamut -60, Omnis -58, Trema -52, Natus -47 (Sin -302/-473 and Vegnagun -217 are colossus framings)
issues.detail: cameraTable: the lateral gap between party and enemy lines is 1.8 to 4.1 world units in x while the depth gap is 3.4 to 8.7 in z, so at FOV 32 the boss lands behind the party on screen. Ch VII: Rikku stands between the two Guado Guardians with a spear crossing her body; Ch VIII: Rikku stands inside Evrae's coils; Ch III: Yuna sits inside the Final Aeon's Left-Arm Strike. The approved targeting B tile shows the party clear of the enemy group. Consequence seen in targeting: the documented x-ray fallback (option C, which Bailey did not pick) fades overlapping party figures to 0.35 while a Guardian is aimed (events: tidus:0.35 x17, rikku:0.35 x8 in Ch VII). The characters lens's stronger claim, that Tidus is ghosted during his own Overdrive, was REFUTED by its skeptic (the strip shows him opaque) and is dropped. Verified (medium) by the camera skeptic from the frames and the cameraTable.
issues.fixHint: Staging, not motion (calm camera and pinned HUD stay): widen lanes in x and pull the enemy depth forward, with a minimum screen gap (about 3 % of frame width, ~48 px at 1600x900) asserted by a unit test over every chapter's projected boxes at 1600x900 and 390x844, colossus chapters exempt. Then limit xray() to anchored multi-part machines and never the acting party member. Show Bailey framing options first (rule 9; EC-1001-05).

issues.title: Den of Woe renders as a near-black void with four-point star flares, far from Bailey's picked O-3 A frame
issues.where: Ch XV Den of Woe, idle, wide (no HUD) and victory, 1600x900
issues.detail: Approved O-3 A (2026-09-25): a cold teal cave with visible rock walls, a lit teal floor and soft round orb motes. Build: walls gone, floor a dark navy grid, motes rendered as hard four-point star flares although the plate prompt excluded 'stars, star shape, sparkles'. Round 15 (before eye candy D) was already dark but stayed teal with round motes, so D's grade and lens flare are suspected to make it worse. A clipped cyan block at the right edge was not confirmed by the skeptic (HUD covers that region). Verified (medium).
issues.fixHint: A per-room override in the D room specs: exposure and black-point lift for den-of-woe so the plate's teal reads, A's star streaks off in this room (round motes only). Acceptance: end-state-board --pair against a-frame.jpg shows walls, no four-point flares; check CINEMA LIGHT on and off.
issues.introducedByCandidate: suspected (eye candy D first shipped in release 33; the darkness predates D, the star flares do not)

issues.title: KO'd FFX-2 girls stay standing (and smiling) when their dressphere has no KO painting
issues.where: Ch XIII Trema defeat, Ch VI, and every FFX-2 chapter whose loadout includes Rikku Dark Knight, Paine Warrior and the other dresspheres without a ko state
issues.detail: Trema defeat frame: Yuna (Dark Knight) and Rikku (Alchemist) show 0 HP in the party panel but stand upright in their idle paintings; Rikku is smiling. The event log has setPose('ko') and fall() at 204873 ms. PaintedActor.fall() (lines ~1425-1448) tips the figure, then tweens fallTilt and fallDrop back to 0, so with no 'ko' painting the idle returns upright. About half of the FFX-2 dresspheres in public/art/manifest.json have no 'ko' state (the lens's exact list is muddled; recount before fixing). FFX is unaffected: every FFX party member has a KO painting. A standing figure at 0 HP misstates the battle state. Verified (medium).
issues.fixHint: Presentation only: when a subject has no 'ko' state, play the existing lieDown roll on the idle (LieFlat.ts, used for Seymour, D-046) with a dim or desaturate tint, reversed on revive, in a small helper module (PaintedActor.ts is over 400 lines and must not grow, rule 7). Acceptance: Trema seed 1 defeat frame shows Yuna DK and Rikku AL down; a Phoenix Down raises them.

issues.title: KO paintings render at the wrong scale against the standing figure (Yuna FFX about 1.6 to 2x; Rikku Black Mage about 0.6x)
issues.where: Ch I Seymour Flux (Yuna KO, FFX; on the phone her body covers Kimahri's station and sits under the Tidus row of the party panel), Ch VI Leblanc (Yuna Gunner and Rikku Black Mage KO, FFX-2), milder for Tidus in Ch I and VIII
issues.detail: In the Ch I strip the prone Yuna's head is about 100 px wide against ~50 px standing, so she reads as a giant beside Kimahri. Cause: computePoseScale (PaintedScale.ts) sizes every pose from idle's pixels-per-unit and only trims it with a sidecar 'scale'; yuna/ko.png was painted at a closer zoom and ko.json has no 'scale', and the maxExtent clamp (2.2x figure height) does not catch it. D-194 dressphere installs got head-matched scales; the FFX party KO paintings never did. Rikku Black Mage's KO goes the other way (a doll-sized body). The art is approved; its on-screen scale is wrong. Verified (medium) in code and strip.
issues.fixHint: Head-match each KO painting against its idle (the D-194 method) and apply the result from a src-side per-pose scale table, not by editing public/art sidecars. Keep the KO body inside its own station. Acceptance: KO head width within 10 % of the standing head in the Ch I and Ch VI KO strips; no party-panel pixels over a KO figure.

issues.title: Every physical attack is one shared 1.4-unit air swing, and the target recoils after the attacker is almost home
issues.where: All chapters, every party and enemy physical action including Overdrives; 1600x900 and phone
issues.detail: BattlePresenterBeats.ts line ~67 gives every 'attack' pose lunge(1.4, 440) and squash(260, 0.45) with no per-command or per-character profile; the target's reaction waits on the windUp sleep, not the lunge apex. Measured across 15 event logs, lunge start to recoil: median 392-399 ms in FFX, 366-369 ms in FFX-2, when the attacker is ~90 % of the way home. Outliers: Spiral Cut 2.0 s, Left-Arm Strike up to 4.1 s, Leblanc 'Attack' 3.8 s. A Gunner lunges forward to fire pistols. The originals connect on contact. Verified (medium) in code and the Tidus strip; the 'swing at air' wording is overstated for melee where the lunge reaches.
issues.fixHint: Fire the damage beat (recoil, numeral, hit-stop) on the lunge's ATTACK_IMPACT frame; give the lunge a per-command profile (melee closes most of the screen gap with no camera whip, ranged fires in place with a recoil kick). Acceptance: lunge apex to recoil within 0-30 ms in every log. Richer choreography is EC-1001-04.

issues.title: Yuna White Mage changes costume and staff between her idle and every action painting

issues.detail: idle.png is a hooded white robe with a red sawtooth hem and a round lattice wand; attack, cast, hurt, ko and victory.png show a white, pink and blue long dress, a small pink hood-scarf, lighter auburn hair and a golden crook staff. None of the yuna-white-mage paintings are pinned in approved-hashes.json; the sources do not settle which costume is canon (rule 6), so Bailey picks the look. Verified (high) by two skeptics.
issues.fixHint: Show Bailey both looks side by side at in-game size; re-render the losing set from the winner's idle sidecar (identity from the shipped idle, body-only pose tags, OpenPose; pilot 3-5 before a batch). Candidates only, to D:/Tools/pyrefly-art-backup/candidates/2026-10-01-max/.

issues.where: Ch V Vegnagun (link 1 Tail), every hit and the KO, all sizes
issues.detail: At rest the Tail is the approved option-A steel painting (D-044 recoloured the green blade to steel). issues.fixHint: Render hurt and KO candidates from the 09-24 idle's sidecar (candidates folder, Bailey picks). Interim, presentation only: fall back to idle plus the procedural recoil for any pose whose generation differs from idle's, and add a test that each pose sidecar matches idle's generation or is listed as deliberate.

issues.title: FFX-2 Bahamut's hurt and KO paintings are a different dragon and are cut flat by their canvas edges
issues.where: Ch IV Bahamut, every hurt and the KO, 1600x900 and phone
issues.detail: Idle: a dark navy dragon with red wings, standing. hurt.png: a blue and violet crouching dragon with a different head and wing shape; ko.png purple. issues.title: Most bosses and adds own 1 to 3 paintings, so their attacks, casts and hits re-show the idle
issues.where: Ch V Vegnagun (Leg, Body, Head idle only; Shuyin idle only), Ch IV Bahamut (no attack or cast), Ch XIII Paragon and Trema, Ch VI Leblanc trio and Fem-Goon, Ch VII Guado Guardians, Ch X Natus, Ch XII Omnis, Sin

issues.detail: seymour-flux-body/idle.png is a crouched Seymour with short spiked silver-blue hair in a plain blue robe; attack, cast, hurt and ko.png show long flowing cyan hair and tattered red and black robes in a saturated poster style. issues.title: The Ixion (Djose) plate is painted from high above but the camera looks almost level, so the figures do not stand on the ground

issues.title: The spherechange flash draws as a solid white rectangle the size of the plane
issues.where: FFX-2 spherechange, first ~0.25 s, Ch IV and Ch VI at 1600x900, 2 of 2 runs
issues.detail: At t=0.00 the girl is replaced by an opaque soft-edged white card on her ground ring; by 0.25 s the new dressphere is drawn normally. The shader's flash is alpha-weighted (PaintedShader.ts ~194-202), so a figure flash cannot make a card; suspected (not traced): the flash runs while setArt is still loading and an unmasked or placeholder texture is on screen (BattlePresenterEvents.ts ~370-377). Verified (medium) from the Leblanc sheet; brief and partly under the 180 ms screen flash, but it reads as a placeholder at FFX-2's signature moment.
issues.fixHint: Preload the destination dressphere's pose map before the flash starts and keep the flash alpha-masked with the discard; swap under a figure-shaped flash. Check with a 16 ms frame series. Fold into the VP-1001-01 build.

issues.title: The Overdrive timing overlay shows a hard-coded move name: Spiral Cut chosen, overlay says 'Slice & Dice'
issues.where: Every FFX chapter: Tidus Swordplay, Auron Bushido and Wakka Slots overlays
issues.detail: Ch VII sheet: overlay titled 'Slice & Dice - SWORDPLAY' while the engine log reads abilityName 'Spiral Cut'. src/battle/ffx/overdrive.ts minigameParams builds { abilityId, timerMs, ... } and never a name; TidusTiming.ts:23 falls back to 'Slice & Dice', AuronSequence.ts:29 to 'Dragon Fang', WakkaReels.ts:27 to 'Slots'. Wrong information at the Overdrive's headline moment. Interface, not visual. Verified (high) in code.
issues.fixHint: Add name: def.name to the minigameParams base (FFX only; check docs/CONTRACTS.md for the event shape, rule 2) and a unit test per overlay asserting the chosen ability's name; real-key check with Spiral Cut, Energy Rain and Shooting Star.

issues.title: Eye candy D's key rim is sized in texels, so low-density bosses get a thick pale sticker halo (Vegnagun ~5 px, ~10 px at 2x) and dark bosses and summons read as black cut-outs with a neon edge
issues.where: Every chapter with CINEMA LIGHT on; worst Ch V Vegnagun, Ch III BFA (pale pink in a red plate), Ch IV Bahamut, Ch XI Shiva, summoned aeons in Ch I and III
issues.detail: rimWidth is in texels (3.4 from BattlePresenterStage, x1.35 under A7), so on screen it scales with 1/texel density: party figures (3-4.7 texels/px) get ~1 px, Vegnagun (0.91; 0.45 at 2x) ~5-10 px. The KeyRim colour lifts the key to luma 0.85, near white in saturated scenes, and bloom (0.66) adds to it. The approved Vegnagun staging A has no halo. Bahamut's cyan rim in the approved D target is fine at its size. Introduced with D in release 33; the switch can turn it off.
issues.fixHint: Width in screen pixels (per-actor texel density or fwidth on alpha), ~1.5 px everywhere; keep saturation (luma ~0.7); cap strength under 1.5 texels/px; an ambient lift for near-black figures. Before/after on Ch III, IV, V with ?fxsub=-a.

issues.title: Light matte halos are baked round several boss paintings (residue from background removal)
issues.where: Ch V Vegnagun, Ch IV Bahamut, Ch III BFA, Ch VIII Evrae, Ch XVII Sin whale; also the Seymour Omnis, Natus and Flux paintings (+37 to +45 luma rings)
issues.detail: A light rim 4 to 15 px wide with stair-stepped outer edges stays with all three D looks off, so it is baked into the art. BFA, Evrae and Sin are approved, so the fix must not touch their pixels.
issues.fixHint: A shader-side defringe in the figure material (switchable, default on): colour-decontaminate texels within 2 texels of alpha < 0.9, or a per-subject 'edgeErode' from a src-side table. Measure on the alpha-edge panels.

issues.title: Figures are hard alpha-cut planes with MSAA off: single-pixel stair-steps on blades, staffs and hair that crawl under sway and lunge
issues.where: Every figure; clearest on Brotherhood, Yuna's staff, Rikku DK's greatsword, Ormi's shield, Vegnagun at 2x
issues.detail: antialias false, composer target samples 0, discard at alphaCut ~0.02, no alpha-to-coverage, and almost every source painting has a binary alpha mask. Party interiors are crisp (3.1-4.7 texels/px), so the edge is the weakest pixel on screen.
issues.fixHint: Alpha-to-coverage with 4x MSAA on the figure pass, or a 1-1.5 px smoothstep feather on filtered alpha, or SMAA after bloom; gate by LOW EFFECTS and measure uncapped p95 (desktop D-on today 1.2-2.9 ms).

issues.title: Pose swaps double-expose two different paintings for 120 to 140 ms
issues.where: Every pose change; clearest Ch IV Bahamut hurt (0.52 s), Ch III BFA attack and hurt (0.71-0.76 s), Yu Pagoda, Ch I Tidus hurt (0.50 s), Ch VI Yuna attack
issues.detail: quadInOut crossfades (party 120 ms, enemy 140 ms) blend paintings with very different silhouettes while the plane moves; strips catch translucent ghosts of both. FFX-2's tempo especially suits cuts.
issues.fixHint: Cut on the hit-flash or a 1-frame ink pop when the silhouette change is large (IoU < ~0.6); keep short blends for idle to ready. Per game: FFX may keep 60-80 ms, FFX-2 cuts. Behind a switch.

issues.title: Element hit tints flood the struck figure with one flat colour, apparently past the approved 0.35 actor-flash cap
issues.where: Ch I Seymour under Fire, Ch X Tidus, Ch XII Wakka (Watera), Ch VIII Wakka (Photon Spray), Ch VI Rikku, Ch V Vegnagun, Ch XV Yuna; phone too
issues.detail: At the hit frame the whole figure goes to one tone and the face is lost; it happens with D off, so it is the base tint. Spell-fx option B (approved) says 'actor flash capped at 0.35'. Peak frames only, uniform not read: medium confidence. Matters for PR-0032 (no REDUCE FLASHES row).
issues.fixHint: Read the hurt-tint uniform at its peak and clamp to 0.35 as an additive element overlay that keeps hue, decaying over ~250 ms with an impact-side rim. Acceptance: hue variance inside the figure at peak at least 50 % of rest.

issues.title: CINEMA LIGHT crushes the rearmost FFX-2 girl (Paine) to a near-silhouette
issues.where: Ch IV, XV, XVI at 1600x900 and 390x844 with D on
issues.detail: Same frozen frame: D off shows Paine's grey-lit face and red outfit; D on leaves an outline on the dark plate, a shadow behind Rikku's sword on the phone. Rikku DK's black armour suffers too. Introduced with D in release 33.
issues.fixHint: A floor on key and fill per party figure under Cinema Light so the rearmost face stays within ~70 % of the frontmost face's luminance; ships under the A switch.

issues.title: Rikku washes out to pink-white over the bright Ch V plate (bloom)
issues.where: Ch V Vegnagun, resting frame, 1600x900
issues.detail: Over the light part of the plate (luminance 0.756) her face and upper body bloom out; the party is 16-19 % of the frame by design (option A), so each figure needs every pixel. The approved option A frame shows the girls crisp.
issues.fixHint: Clamp party-figure luminance before the bloom threshold (0.66) or mask figures out of the bloom pass.

issues.title: A translucent haze box shows behind Yunalesca's attack painting
issues.where: Yunalesca chapter, her attack pose (Dispelling Slap), 1600x900
issues.detail: A lighter, faintly blue rectangle ~310 px wide stands behind her with a hard left edge: low-alpha canvas pixels survive the 0.02 alpha cut. yunalesca-1 is approved, so the fix is in the renderer.
issues.fixHint: A per-subject alpha floor (0.08-0.15) from a src-side table, or smoothstep(floor, floor+0.1, a) in the figure shader; a lint flagging poses whose sub-0.15 alpha covers > 5 % of the canvas.

issues.title: Victory framing cuts party members (Ch III Lulu and Yuna); Ch VII's Seymour 'body' shot looks down 24.65 degrees on a flat card with the party out of frame before swinging back
issues.where: Ch III and Ch VII victory moment, 1600x900
issues.detail: Ch III victory: Lulu cut at the left edge, Yuna's feet off-frame. Ch VII: frames at camera (1.30, 4.60, 4.62), 24.65-degree pitch, show the fallen Seymour as a thin card with only Rikku's head in frame, and the Yuna victory strip shows a ~0.75-1.5 s swing back to the party. CONTESTED: the fidelity skeptic found the registered Ch VII victory rig (src/scenes/macalania-temple.ts) is ~11 degrees and the manifest labels the steep frame 'rig body', so the steep shot is the Seymour 'body' departure rig before victory, not the victory rig itself. Prove by a real-key run (rule 3) before fixing.
issues.fixHint: Frame body and party together (pitch at most ~12 degrees, every living party member inside a 5 % safe area) and cut, not swing, into the victory rig (D-291). A test asserting every living party box inside the safe area in the victory state.

issues.title: FFX action pushes grow the party from 35 to 48 % and cut figures at the frame edge or under the party panel
issues.where: Ch III overdrive and enemy action, Ch VII enemy action (Tidus boots cut) and overdrive (Valefor cut), Ch VIII hit, Yojimbo hit; 1600x900
issues.detail: cameraStates log figures cut by the frame; the enlargement goes to feet and HUD overlap rather than the actor. FFX-2's action rig stays at 31-37 % and clips nothing.
issues.fixHint: A framing clamp on push rigs: every on-field figure inside a 5 % safe rect and above the party panel's top; push toward the acting figure, not the party centroid.

issues.title: PR-0002 acceptance still fails in Ch III: the 5-row FFX command stack covers part of Tidus (party slot 0)
issues.where: Ch III Braska's Final Aeon, command menu and target states, 1600x900
issues.detail: Approved tile PR-0002 (D-041) mustChange: move party slot 0 right so its quad clears the stack's footprint. The WHITE MAGIC, ITEMS and FLEE slabs cover a strip of Tidus's lower legs and feet (skeptic: ~15-25 % of the figure, not the lens's 35-40 %); head, torso and sword stay visible. Other FFX chapters clip only a sword tip or staff. Skeptic downgraded from major to polish.
issues.fixHint: Apply approved option A in Ch III's slot data; add the stack-overlap check (stage.projectRect against the panel rects setPanels publishes) for all FFX chapters.

issues.title: Mortiorchis stays standing through Seymour Flux's death and the victory camera
issues.where: Ch I, defeat into victory (adv run), 1600x900
issues.detail: After Flux's pillar and pyrefly dissolve, Mortiorchis stays fully opaque and idle from 1.01 s to at least 2.52 s, in frame as the camera swings to the party. Its own kill, drain and re-form cycle is presented well (FC-3).
issues.fixHint: On the battle-result event dissolve every remaining enemy, staggered 150-250 ms after the boss; a test that no enemy has alpha > 0 when the victory rig begins.

issues.title: Summoned aeons are staged over the boss and render as dark rim-lit silhouettes (Bahamut in Ch I and III)
issues.where: Ch I and Ch III summon entrance (2 s after the event), 1600x900
issues.detail: Bahamut hides Mortiorchis and half of Seymour in Ch I and half of BFA in Ch III, near-black with a cyan (I) or magenta (III) rim, so the arrival reads as a silhouette collision. Valefor in Ch II is staged well on the party side. The glyph entrance (research §7) may have passed before the 2 s still (UNVERIFIED).
issues.fixHint: Anchor wide aeons to the party third (right bound left of the boss's left bound), an ambient lift during the entrance, the per-aeon glyph ring under them. Acceptance: aeon and boss overlap at most 5 % in I, III and X.

issues.title: Ch XI at rest: the floor plate ends 25 to 30 px above the frame bottom, leaving a flat violet band
issues.where: Ch XI Fallen Aeons, resting camera and idle, hit and spell frames, 1600x900
issues.detail: The cracked-rock floor stops on a slanted line at y ~862-876; below it is an untextured violet fill (row std ~6). Same class as PR-0300 (Ch XV seam band) but at rest. Suspected: B's DepthPlates geometry does not cover the frustum bottom here.
issues.fixHint: Compare ?fx=off and ?fxsub=-b at the same frame to find the layer, then extend the plate. A test that the floor covers the bottom 2 % of every chapter's rest frame at 1600x900 and 390x844.

issues.title: Trema casts rectangular shadow slabs instead of figure-shaped shadows
issues.where: Ch XIII Trema, wide and spell, 1600x900
issues.detail: Behind Rikku and Paine a soft dark parallelogram the size of the sprite quad lies on the floor. Suspected: this room's cast-shadow light projects the plane's bounds rather than its alpha.
issues.fixHint: alphaTest on the shadow (customDepthMaterial) or the blob contact shadow in this room.

issues.title: HUD layers draw over the splash band and its title; FFX-2's CHARGING slab still covers 'MEGA' (D must-fix 6 not met)
issues.where: Every cut-in: FFX I, III, IX, X, XIV, XVII; FFX-2 IV and XVI; 1600x900
issues.detail: FFX: the dimmed turn order and ghosted enemy card print through 'MEGA FLARE' and 'ENERGY RAY'; the Yojimbo plate is cut by the top letterbox. FFX-2 Ch IV: the CHARGING 0 slab sits over 'MEGA'; the approved D must-fix 6 says the title sits clear, and its own proof (fix-6-splash-title.jpg) still shows MEGA under the slab. Ch XVI: the open guide panel overlaps the band. Also Tidus's active chip stays at full opacity over Kimahri's splash while the rest fades (Ch I).
issues.fixHint: Fade HUD-avoid elements (turn order, enemy card, CHARGING, guide, the active chip) to 0 during the splash or raise the splash z; opacity only, nothing moves (D-291). Acceptance: zero HUD pixels over the band rect in the I, IV, IX and XVI cut-ins.

issues.title: Sin's clock, Mouth Open card and status smoke draw opaque over Auron's Dragon Fang splash
issues.where: Ch XVIII Sin Face, Auron Overdrive cut-in, 1600x900
issues.detail: '7 TURNS LEFT', 'MOUTH OPEN 1 OF 3' and the pips stay at full opacity near Auron's face; status smoke renders in front of the band. Widens PR-0271 from party actions to the splash.
issues.fixHint: Same layering rule as VP-1001-32; no clock or smoke pixels inside the band rect.

issues.title: The boss figure covers the FFX-2 splash title (Ixion over 'AEROSPARK')
issues.where: Ch XVI Aerospark cut-in, 1600x900 and 390x844
issues.detail: The approved D splash frame has the title clear above Ixion's back; at f302f163 the must-fix 6 move put it mid-slab and Ixion's body draws in front: only 'AEROS' reads.
issues.fixHint: Draw the title above the figure layer or place it away from the boss's projected bounds per chapter.

issues.title: HUD cards cover boss figures at rest and the status line overprints the FFX-2 intent ability name
issues.where: Ch I (Mortiorchis card over Seymour Flux, PR-0248 class, FFX), Ch IV (intent card over Bahamut's wing), Ch VI (intent card over Ormi), Ch XV ('Paine was stopped.' over 'Glint'); 1600x900
issues.detail: Carried classes PR-0249 and PR-0248, re-found by three lenses.
issues.fixHint: Status line in its own slot below the intent card; enemy figure rects added to the hudAvoid set.

issues.title: Phone cut-ins: the title is near-invisible, ghost intent text prints over the art, and the Thundara flash lifts the slice to a milky veil
issues.where: 390x844: Ch I Mighty Guard, Ch IV Mega Flare, Ch XVI Aerospark cut-ins; Ch VII Thundara
issues.detail: 'MIGHTY GUARD' and 'MEGA FLARE' render as pale grey at ~15 % opacity (possibly caught mid fade-in); the ghost intent line prints over Kimahri's hair. During Thundara the whole battle slice turns grey-white and the intent card goes low-contrast; desktop spell frames keep their blacks.
issues.fixHint: Hold full-opacity dark ink from the slab's settle; hide ghost HUD under the band; cap phone screen-flash opacity (~0.35) and add it before the grade. Acceptance: title contrast >= 4.5:1 at 300 ms; spell frame black level within 10 luma of rest.

issues.title: Results portraits show a white alpha fringe; the phone results caption is still clipped
issues.where: Results, Ch I 1600x900 (Tidus) and Ch XVI 390x844
issues.detail: Tidus's hair spikes carry a 1-2 px white matte line with stair-stepping; 'DJOSE TEMPLE - CHAMBER OF THE I...' is clipped (PR-0250 re-confirmed).
issues.fixHint: Premultiply or 1 px defringe at load without touching approved pixels; fit or wrap the caption.

issues.title: A KO'd Auron (0/3410) stands upright in the Ch I victory frame (UNVERIFIED)
issues.where: Ch I victory, advisor run that ended in an injected autoBattle hand-off, 1600x900
issues.detail: One frame, from an injected hand-off path; whether a switch-in or the hand-off causes it is not traced. Prove by running the presenter (rule 3) before fixing.
issues.fixHint: Trace setPose('ko') against the victory pose fan-out; HP 0 members keep their KO pose through victory; a presenter test.

issues.title: Seymour's Ch VII defeat tips his standing painting flat into a stretched plank
issues.where: Ch VII Seymour KO and departure, 1600x900
issues.detail: seymour-macalania has no KO painting; lieDown rotates the idle 90 degrees into a dark board with a foreshortened face, no reflection or contact shadow, at the chapter's climax. The 'body' departure is canon (research §3.2); the read is cardboard. Related to PR-0244. Note: commit 30f2319c installed approved Seymour kneel/fall poses today; check whether they cover seymour-macalania before rendering anything.
issues.fixHint: If not covered: a fallen and a kneel candidate for seymour-macalania (Bailey picks). Interim: never lay an idle flat; sink-and-dim the upright figure (a test that lieDown refuses subjects without a KO painting, except the party fallback of VP-1001-04).

issues.title: Pose paintings drift in identity: Yuna Gunner's hurt is a different costume and her hair goes auburn to red; Rikku shrinks on hurt
issues.where: Ch VI Leblanc and XIII Trema (Yuna Gunner hurt, attack, victory, KO); Ch VI Rikku hurt
issues.detail: The approved Gunner idle (cast:yuna-gunner, pinned) has dark brown hair; her victory, hurt and KO paintings are auburn or orange, pushed red by the magenta plates; the hurt painting wears a long pink and white skirt instead of the Gunner shorts. Rikku's hurt still is shorter and turned to camera.
issues.fixHint: Re-render the drifting poses from the approved idle sidecar as candidates (yuna-gunner is pinned: Bailey's word needed). Cheap interim behind a switch: a per-pose colour match to the idle and content-box height normalisation at load.

issues.title: Kimahri is painted with two intact side horns; the sourced broken forehead horn is missing
issues.where: Every chapter with Kimahri; idle figure and Mighty Guard splash
issues.detail: research/visual-bible.md §1.6 (FF Wiki, single source): a broken horn on his forehead. The battle painting shows two curved intact side horns; the splash one long intact horn. Kimahri's cast group has no verdict yet, but commit 30f2319c installed Bailey's approved Kimahri kneels today, so check the pinned set before proposing a re-render.
issues.fixHint: A candidate idle with a single broken forehead-horn stub from §1.6, then poses from it; Bailey picks.

issues.title: Vegnagun Tail and Sin paintings are magnified and soft at their staged size (Vegnagun 0.91 texels/px, 0.45 at 2x)
issues.where: Ch V Tail at 96 % of frame; Ch XVII Sin fin 1.22 and Ch XVIII Sin face 1.24 texels/px at 1600x900 (~0.6 at 2x, inferred)
issues.detail: The 1176x822 Tail painting is the biggest figure in the game and the softest: rivets smear and the silhouette steps at 3200x1800. D-228 staging is right; the source resolution is wrong. Sin is approved art; the Tail and Sin fins are free to re-render.
issues.fixHint: 2x candidates (>= 2352 px long side) regenerated or upscaled against the shipped painting, as @2x variants the loader picks when projected height exceeds the texture height; approved 1x stays untouched; Bailey's okay required.

issues.title: Colossal bosses render near party height: BFA 1.13x Tidus, Natus 0.96 (24 % of frame against ~60 % in its approved frame), Bahamut 1.42, Yunalesca 1.51, Evrae 1.66
issues.where: Ch III BFA, Ch X Natus, Ch IV Bahamut, Yunalesca, Ch VIII Evrae; resting camera, 1600x900
issues.detail: Only Sin (2.6-3.1x) and Vegnagun (5.5x, D-228) feel colossal. Evrae's distance is the mechanic (research §8, §9.11) and it is coiled on the deck among the party; BFA and Bahamut scale is from knowledge, unsourced. Bailey's Natus pick named the painting, not the scale. BFA's attack painting is also a different palette (orange-red fur, blue armour) from its dark idle (approved: Bailey's question), and its lunge passes behind the near Yu Pagoda.
issues.fixHint: Option D for Bailey (EC-1001-05): per-boss colossus profiles (the Vegnagun A method, low camera, 1.6-2.2x party height), Evrae off the deck at range; ask about BFA's attack palette. Non-art fix now: raise the attacker's renderOrder during a lunge.

issues.title: Party members overlap each other: the stair-step formation hides the third member
issues.where: Every chapter; worst Ch XII Omnis (Auron ~80 % hidden), X Natus, I Flux (Kimahri), IV Bahamut and XVI Ixion (Paine behind Rikku's greatsword); worse on the phone
issues.detail: A diagonal echelon at fixed 37/31/27 % heights in almost every chapter (Den of Woe and Fallen Aeons share identical lane offsets). The approved targeting B tile shows three separated figures.
issues.fixHint: Spread lanes so each member is >= 70 % unoccluded at rest, asserted from projected boxes; looser for FFX-2 (free positions, research §9), tighter for FFX. Show before/after for XII and IV.

issues.title: Far master in Ch IX Yojimbo and Ch X Natus: everyone ~25 % of the frame over dark empty floor
issues.where: Ch IX and X resting camera (FOV 28, y 5.1, z 17.6, pitch 10.6 degrees), 1600x900
issues.detail: Horizon at ~12 % of frame; Daigoro 64 px; ~60 % of the frame is unlit floor or upper architecture. The battlefield reads but nobody has presence; push-ins then put the party under the HUD.
issues.fixHint: Bring both into the house framing (FOV 32-34, party >= 33 %) or keep the wide only as an establishing shot; include in the options round.

issues.title: The pinned HUD leaves a middle strip ~45 % wide and the composition does not lens-shift into it
issues.where: All chapters at the command menu, 1600x900; clearest Ch I, XII, II, IV
issues.detail: Command stack x ~40-620, party rows ~1000-1550 by 640-870, turn list on the right; party feet sit in the rows' band. The scene's framing is the same with or without the HUD. Root of how depth stacking turns into overlap.
issues.fixHint: A static per-layout camera.setViewOffset centring party plus boss in the HUD-free rectangle (no motion; comfort unchanged), computed from the hudAvoid rects. Pair with VP-1001-02.

issues.title: Defeats look different within one fight, and FFX-2's living Syndicate goons burst into pyreflies
issues.where: Ch VI Leblanc (Ormi fades; Dr. Goon and Fem-Goon get the pillar and pyreflies); Ch VII Guado Guardians (plain fade)
issues.detail: presentation §3.2 names Leblanc, Logos and Ormi as living humans who must not dissolve; D-035 named only the three, so the goons stay on 'dissolve'. Whether the goons and the Guardians are 'living' is our inference: ask Bailey. The approved 'Dissolved into pyreflies, not faded out' tile covers fiends.
issues.fixHint: A per-game defeat table (fiend or unsent: pyrefly erosion; living FFX: collapse plus fade; living FFX-2: knockback and retreat) from research, Bailey settling the cases the sources do not; a two-line DEPARTURE_KINDS change for the goons if he says yes (FFX-2 only).

issues.title: Ice spell crystals are flat low-poly CG shards that hide the target through the whole hurt
issues.where: Ch VI Blizzard on the girls (FFX-2), Ch X Blizzard on Tidus (FFX), 1600x900
issues.detail: The only clearly 3D-CG element against painted figures, opaque in front of the face 0.0-0.7 s. Spell-fx option B is approved, so a look question.
issues.fixHint: Option: painted texture or soft rim on the shards, ~0.6 opacity, drawn behind the upper body.

issues.title: No per-game motion tempo: FFX-2 attacks and casts run on FFX timings (casts even slower)
issues.where: All FFX-2 chapters, attack and cast
issues.detail: lunge 440 ms/1.4 and squash 260 ms/0.45 are identical in both games; cast dwell median 1773 ms FFX vs 1973 ms FFX-2. The sources say only that FFX-2 is faster ATB; a snappier motion tempo is our reading.
issues.fixHint: Option: FFX-2 lunge ~300 ms and cast holds ~1.0-1.2 s; measured against the pacing ratios so the friends' 'too fast' note (2026-09-29) is not reopened.

issues.title: Yuna Dark Knight and Rikku Alchemist idles face the viewer straight on, and the Dark Knight reads as pastel armour
issues.where: Ch XIII Trema and any chapter using these dresspheres
issues.detail: No visual source for the Dark Knight look (rule 6); dressphere idles have no verdict yet. The approved Gunner is also frontal, so frontal is not a defect in itself.
issues.fixHint: One sheet of the FFX-2 dressphere idles at in-game size for Bailey; record the reaction in a tile.

issues.title: Ch III Tidus showed no Overdrive row with a full gauge on steered turns (UNVERIFIED; combat lens)
issues.where: Ch III Braska's Final Aeon, steered run
issues.detail: The gauge was injected to 100, so it may be a capture artifact. Not proven by running the engine; routed to the combat lens.
issues.fixHint: Set the gauge through the real path in the pure engine and check the command list; if missing, trace BFA's command filter.

gaps.title: Living figures: visible idle life for party and bosses (breathing, hair and cloth, wings and tails)
gaps.detail: Today breathe 0.016 at 0.4 Hz and sway 0.009-0.012 (~2 px) on a rigid plane: 8 idle frames over 2 s are indistinguishable for Yuna, Rikku and Bahamut, and casts and victories hold one still for 1.8-3.6 s. The originals idle constantly; the visual bible authors per-character idle personality (Auron still, Rikku bouncing, Kimahri a 2 px breath). Options: (a) mesh-bend or 2-bone deformation of the painted plane from an auto-derived weight mask, (b) a separate hair/cape layer per idle, (c) per-character amplitude and tempo profiles with no new art. A soft re-offer of 'cutout-animation' (declined 19 Sep): label it so. Own switch, default on (D-297); REDUCE MOTION stills it. Enemy variant: vertex-weighted wing, tail and head regions.

gaps.title: Painted art inside every aeon Overdrive and boss Special splash (today a blank cream or pink slab)
gaps.detail: Party Overdrives carry a painted portrait (Mighty Guard, Dragon Fang); every aeon Overdrive (Energy Ray, Mega Flare in III, VII, IX, X, XIV, XVII) and FFX-2's boss Specials (Mega Flare, Aerospark) show an empty band across ~45 % of the frame. Cheapest route needs no new paintings: the approved boss or aeon attack/cast still, cropped by a per-figure focal box with the party splash's parallax slide. Whether an FFX-2 boss Special gets art at all is decided from research/ffx-vs-ffx2-presentation.md.

gaps.title: Per-move Overdrive choreography (Spiral Cut leap and dive, Slice & Dice dashes, Banishing Blade) instead of the plain Attack lunge
gaps.detail: poseForCommand maps 'overdrive' to 'attack'; the only difference from Attack is the cut-in. RE-OFFER of 'overdrive-cinematic' (declined 19 Sep): (a) 2-4 reference-locked paintings plus plane motion inside the calm rules, (b) VFX-only signature trails, (c) leave as is. Short or skip after first viewing.

gaps.title: Attack anticipation, contact hold, follow-through and enemy reach
gaps.detail: Beyond the timing defect VP-1001-06: a 90 ms anticipation crouch, 2-3 after-image ghosts on the lunge path (Spectacle sub-switch), a 60 ms contact hold, then recoil; enemy melee reaching toward the target lane (capped at 40 % of the gap; Ormi's Shield Bash plays from the back wall today); the rig held on the attacker until contact. REDUCE MOTION drops ghosts and distance.

gaps.title: Authored per-chapter framings: four options for camera perspective (A across the field, B three-quarter hero, C HD-2D tilt diorama, D colossus scale)
gaps.detail: 16 of 18 chapters share one profile master (FOV 32, pitch 1-9 degrees, states differing by 1-2 units of dolly); FFX reframes per action (research §2.1). Sin's deck and Vegnagun A prove what one well-composed master adds. All four are framing, angle and staging only within D-291: static masters and hard cuts, pinned HUD, comfort measured per option against the fb2-0929 table, each with an FFX and an FFX-2 variant (rule 14) and its own switch. Resolves VP-1001-02, -13, -14 and the polish staging items.

gaps.title: Bosses that react: part motion and telegraphs for multi-part bosses (Vegnagun never reframes and never moves)
gaps.detail: Ch V: rig 'idle' in every state (camera moves < 0.04 units); Noli Me Tangere lands with the tail motionless. Options within D-291: (a) a slow 1.5-2 % push toward the tail on its turn, (b) a light-only telegraph (conduits brighten, plate darkens), (c) a tail mesh-warp windup and head bob from the existing part paintings. REDUCE MOTION keeps only (b). Also a calm push toward the acting girl (16-19 % of frame today).

gaps.title: Hero framing for the FFX Overdrive input window
gaps.detail: For the 2.75 s timing window the frame is the resting master with Tidus buried in the enemy cluster behind the timing card. A cut (not a swing) to a prebuilt three-quarter shot with the actor at ~50 % and the target visible, cut back after; HUD pinned; REDUCE MOTION uses the same cut.

gaps.title: Enemy skill travel and impact effects (Tail Beam, Photon Spray, Power Wave)
gaps.detail: Party spells have per-element effects; enemy specials show only the name banner and a hit tint. Extend the option-B registry with an enemy-skill family (beam, breath, shockwave, spray) keyed by ability id with a generic fallback. Present as an option (rule 10).

gaps.title: A KO collapse beat (buckle, sink, cut to the KO painting with a dust or pyrefly puff)
gaps.detail: Today standing at 0.02 s and prone at 0.16 s under a flash. The visual bible authors a 4-frame collapse for the Shuyin-arc figures. No new art: tip the hurt painting 15-25 degrees and sink ~200 ms, then cut. Stilled under REDUCE MOTION.

gaps.title: Keyed victory gestures (Tidus sword toss; sourced FFX-2 dressphere victories)
gaps.detail: Victory is one still held 2.8-3.6 s. The visual bible records Tidus's toss, catch, sweep and shoulder rest and FFX-2 Gunner blowing smoke. 2-3 keyed frames from reference-locked renders, played once and held; the sourced holds in II, IV, V, XIII stay. 'victory-poses-results' was declined 19 Sep as a results redesign; this smaller in-place option is separate.

gaps.title: Figures relit from derived normal or depth maps instead of a fixed rim
gaps.detail: Derive a normal map from each painting's alpha and luminance once at load so CINEMA LIGHT follows form, tinted by the plate's key; removes the sticker-rim tell (VP-1001-17) and lifts dark bosses. GPU-side: affordable on desktop (~5x headroom), gated by LOW EFFECTS on the phone.

gaps.title: Painted Overdrive and Special key poses (charge and release) per party member
gaps.detail: Each party figure has 9 stills and none for the Overdrive; Tidus holds 'ready' for the whole timing window. Pilot Tidus and Yuna, behind the C switch; candidates only.

gaps.title: An FFX-2 battle view of its own (wider lens, looser spread with flank space, cuts not swings)
gaps.detail: FFX-2 masters use FFX's FOV 32 family and near-static states; research §9 gives FFX-2 free battle positions and hard switches into battle view, recommending 'a short, fast, showy reframe'. Measure shot changes per second against the comfort table first.

gaps.title: Phone: the battlefield fills the black lower third during non-input beats
gaps.detail: During actions, spells and cut-ins ~30-40 % of a 390x844 screen is flat black. Render the stage full-height behind a graded scrim so nothing resizes or moves when the menu hides (D-291 kept), or put a static pinned action card in the void. Phone CPU headroom is thin (Ch I p99 33.4 ms under 4x throttle): measure on a real phone.

gaps.title: Per-aeon glyph entrance that persists faintly while the aeon is on the field
gaps.detail: Research §7: each aeon emerges through its own glyph; the 2 s stills could not show it (UNVERIFIED absence). Capture an entrance strip first.

gaps.title: Hybrid 3D figures (a labelled DEPARTURE from the settled painted 2.5D direction)
gaps.detail: Mesh deformation, derived normals and per-limb cutouts reach roughly Octopath-level life; the ceilings of painted planes are turning, lying down, foreshortened lunges and camera orbits. A hybrid is the only route past them. At most one option may show it, clearly labelled as a departure; not recommended without Bailey's explicit pick (AGENTS.md rule 9).

refuted.title: The x-ray fade ghosts Tidus to 35 % during his own Overdrive
refuted.reason: Skeptic: the full-frame strip shows Tidus opaque from 0.25 to 2.75 s; xray() is called only from the HUD target-selection paths. The narrower, real part (party figures fade while an overlapping enemy is aimed) is folded into VP-1001-02.

refuted.title: The Ch VII victory rig is a 24.65-degree high angle
refuted.reason: Skeptic: the registered victory rig in macalania-temple.ts is ~11 degrees; the steep frame is labelled 'rig body'. Kept as a contested polish item (VP-1001-25) because two other lenses saw the steep body shot and the swing back in the strips; to be proven by a real-key run.
